issues.detail: The Greek text says 'τα αλλως εχοντα' (those having other things/works), but the Vietnamese translates this as 'những việc khác' (other works/things). While similar, the Greek specifically refers to 'the [people] having other [works]', whereas the Vietnamese makes it about the 'works' themselves. However, a more significant issue is the omission of the implied subject/possessor.
The Greek 'τα αλλως εχοντα' implies 'those who have other [works]'. The Vietnamese 'những việc khác' omits the possessor, changing the focus from the people/possessors to the objects themselves.
